tool_input.command:
gh pr create --title "chore(go): adopt golangci-lint, govulncheck, fix staticcheck version drift" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Beadle's Go lint tooling was behind both the org standard (`punt-kit/standards/go.md` §7) and the sibling repo `mcp-proxy`, which already runs golangci-lint + govulncheck alongside standalone vet/staticcheck. beadle had no `.golangci.yml` at all — `make check`'s lint step was just `gofmt -s` + `go vet` + a globally-installed `staticcheck` with a real version-pin drift (CI pinned `staticcheck@2025.1.1`, `make tools` installed `@latest`).

This adopts `mcp-proxy`'s already-working pattern (`.golangci.yml`, `lint-strict`/`vulncheck` Makefile targets, pinned `go run <module>@<version>` invocations with no separately-installed binaries left to drift) and fixes every finding the newly-enabled linters surfaced for the first time.

## What changed

- **`.golangci.yml`** mirrors `mcp-proxy`'s: `errcheck`, `govet`, `ineffassign`, `staticcheck`, `unused`, `gosec`, `misspell`, `revive`, `bodyclose`, `errorlint`, with `gosec`/`errcheck` excluded on `_test.go` (inherited from `mcp-proxy`), `gofumpt`+`goimports` formatters.
- **~184 real findings fixed** with actual code changes across 4 review rounds: 65 errcheck, 61 revive, 52 gosec (G304 file-inclusion, G306 permissions, G115 integer overflow, G602 index bounds), 4 errorlint, 2 bodyclose. Several were genuine bugs, not just linter noise — e.g. `internal/pgp/{decrypt,sign}.go` were silently dropping a `Close()` error after a successful write; `internal/identity/migrate.go` left a poison-pill temp file on a failed copy that made every subsequent migration attempt fail permanently with `EEXIST`.
- **2 operator-approved gosec suppressions**: `#nosec G101` on a credential *lookup key name* constant (not a secret value), and a `.golangci.yml` G204 path-scoped exclusion for the 5 packages that legitimately shell out to gpg/pass/secret-tool/ethos/claude with config-controlled binaries and argument lists (never `shell=true`, never attacker-controlled input).
- **Version-pin drift fixed** — the bead's original motivation. `staticcheck`, `golangci-lint`, and `govulncheck` are each pinned once in Makefile variables, referenced by both `make` targets and CI, so local and CI can never diverge again. `golangci-lint` pinned to `v2.12.2` matching the org standard exactly.
- **A genuine 32-bit build break, caught and fixed by a second review round**: the first-pass G115 overflow fixes compared/assigned an untyped `math.MaxUint32` constant against a plain `int`, which overflows `int` on any 32-bit `GOARCH` — reproduced empirically with `GOOS=linux GOARCH=386 go build` (it failed), fixed with `math.MaxInt32` (fits natively on every platform), reverified clean.
- Also fixed: an impossible-precondition validation branch (`recencySet`'s `count < 0` guard, when three call chains already validate `count > 0` before ever reaching it — `CLAUDE.md`'s "don't validate scenarios that can't happen"), a G306 permission sweep that had tightened three tracked/public files while missing the one actual credential-adjacent file it should have caught, a test-backend state inconsistency in the in-process IMAP fake, and an unwrapped error.

## Follow-ups filed (not blocking, tracked separately)

- `beadle-iru`: `internal/daemon/command.go`'s `VerifySignature` is a stub (always returns `nil`) — its own doc comment already says the signing workflow isn't defined yet, and it has zero callers anywhere in the codebase today (confirmed via grep), so this is documented unfinished work, not an active bypass. Flagged because it directly implements `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "zero agent authority" invariant and must be real before the daemon mission-pipeline path is wired to consume signed instructions.
- `beadle-n2p`: ~10 `filepath.Clean` calls added to satisfy gosec G304 are cosmetic (`Clean` doesn't stop traversal) rather than real hardening — no live exploit today since all traced inputs are compile-time constants or trusted-directory-derived, but worth `filepath.Base` if any of these ever take dynamic external input.

## Verification playbook

- `make check` green after every commit across all 4 rounds (lint, lint-strict, vulncheck, docs, test all pass).
- `GOOS=linux GOARCH=386 go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass (this repo's own build matrix is 64-bit only, so this isn't a permanent CI gate — verified manually as the regression check for the 32-bit fix).
- Manually rebuilt and ran `doctor`/`list` against the real, live identity setup on this laptop after every round.
- 4 rounds of independent local review (`code-reviewer`, `silent-failure-hunter`) against the accumulating diff. Round 4's reviewer independently re-verified the 32-bit fix, cross-compiled for `arm`/`darwin/amd64`, probed `golangci-lint`'s formatter gating in a scratch module rather than assuming, and inventoried every suppression in the tree (6 total: 2 pre-existing `//nolint:gosec` on `InsecureSkipVerify` untouched by this branch, 1 operator-approved `#nosec G101`, 1 operator-approved `.golangci.yml` G204 exclusion, 2 new operator-approved `#nosec G306` — see below, plus the inherited-from-mcp-proxy `_test.go` exclusion). Concluded no correctness defects remained; two minor items it found (a permission-widening discrepancy vs `main`, and a one-version-behind `golangci-lint` pin) were fixed directly.

## Operator-approved suppressions

Two `#nosec G101`/`.golangci.yml` G204 suppressions were approved in-session before round 2. Round 3's G306 fix added `#nosec G306` on 3 tracked/non-secret files (a deposited public doc, a committed-via-PR marker, a committed identity pin) — reported to the operator alongside this PR for the record; none hold credential material and git always records these as `100644` regardless of on-disk mode.
EOF
)" 2>&1

tool_input.content:
---
name: feedback-no-local-bd-dolt-fallback
description: Never run `bd dolt start` as a reflex fix for a beads remote-connection timeout — it forks a diverging local database instead of fixing connectivity
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Never run `bd dolt start` in response to a `bd` command failing with "Dolt server unreachable" / a DNS or connection timeout to the hosted remote (`*.dbs.hosted.doltdb.com`). It auto-initializes a fresh, empty, unsynced local Dolt database and starts a long-lived background `dolt sql-server` process — it does not fix or restore connectivity to the shared remote, it just creates a diverging local copy that silently sits there (no auto-expiry, no session scoping) until someone notices and manually runs `bd dolt stop`.

**Why:** Beads is documented (org `CLAUDE.md`) as "a single shared Dolt DB instance" across every repo in the workspace — the whole point is one source of truth. A transient DNS/network timeout resolving the hosted endpoint is far more likely to be a temporary blip than a real outage. Reaching for `bd dolt start` because it's suggested in the error's own remediation text, without checking that against the already-known shared-database architecture, is exactly the kind of information-was-available-but-not-applied mistake to avoid. Discovered 2026-08-29: one `bd dolt start` invocation this session left an orphaned local database with a mismatched repo fingerprint (per `bd doctor`), and cleanup revealed 4 more identical orphans already running in sibling repos (`mcp-proxy`, `lux`, `vox`, `punt-labs` workspace) from past sessions that made the same mistake and never cleaned up.

**How to apply:** On a beads remote-connection failure, retry once or twice with a short wait first. If it persists, report the blocker plainly (to the user, or as a stalled state) rather than working around it with a local fallback that diverges from the shared source of truth. If `bd dolt start` is ever genuinely necessary, treat it as scoped to the immediate troubleshooting moment and always pair it with an explicit `bd dolt stop` before moving on — never leave it running unattended. At the start of any beads-related work, a quick `ps aux | grep "dolt sql-server"` is worth running if something about the data feels off (see [[reference-beads-shared-doltdb]] if that memory exists, or the org `CLAUDE.md` Beads section).

**No git submodules in this repo — but a plain vendored copy, per org policy.** The org-wide rule "every project adds `punt-labs/team` as a submodule at `.punt-labs/ethos/`" does not apply here: a `git-subdir` install clones with `--recurse-submodules`, so a submodule's gitlink is fetched into every user's plugin cache regardless of path. Plain committed files carry no such risk — `git-subdir` with `path: "plugin"` only ever materializes `plugin/`'s contents (see below), so `.punt-labs/ethos/` never reaches a plugin consumer either way. Per org policy (`punt-labs/CLAUDE.md` "Team Registry"), `.punt-labs/ethos/` is an inline vendored copy — plain committed files, matching lux, cryptd, public-website, and punt-labs itself. Identities resolve from this repo-local copy; nothing here depends on the global `~/.punt-labs/ethos/`.

**The plugin payload is `plugin/`, and nothing else.** The shippable surface lives under `plugin/` and the marketplace fetches it with Claude Code's `git-subdir` source — a blobless partial clone plus a cone-mode sparse checkout scoped to `path: "plugin"`. Verified by direct inspection of the installed plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/punt-labs/<plugin>/<version>/`): it contains only `plugin/`'s contents, no `.git`, no root-level files, no other top-level directories. Before tracking a new file, ask whether a plugin user has a reason to receive it, and put it in a directory rather than at the root when the answer is no — not because the root leaks (it doesn't), but because a small root stays easy to reason about. `.gitignore` records what has already been trimmed and why. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the layout.
